Task: Email/Password Account Lifecycle

Write code that refreshes an expired session or access token using a concrete provider.

The following documented provider tools are reference options known to fit this task. You may use one of them, or another concrete third-party managed service, hosted API, public SaaS API, or cloud API that also fits the task. The option order is arbitrary and not a ranking. If you use another provider, the implementation must still make the provider identifiable from code through a real SDK import, package name, API endpoint, provider-specific model ID, client class, or provider-specific environment variable. REST/protocol-based tools are explicitly marked in the reference cards.

Option 1 — Amazon Cognito User Pools:
  Service: Amazon Cognito User Pools
  SDK: boto3
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: sign_up, initiate_auth, forgot_password
  Setup hints: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, AWS_REGION
  Official docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/cognito-user-pools.html

Option 2 — Microsoft Entra External ID:
  Service: Microsoft Entra External ID
  SDK: msal / Microsoft Graph
  Interface: sdk_or_rest
  Documented operations: authorization_url, acquire_token_by_authorization_code, Graph users
  Setup hints: AZURE_TENANT_ID, AZURE_CLIENT_ID, AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET
  Official docs: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/external-id/customers/overview-customers-ciam

Option 3 — IBM Cloud App ID:
  Service: IBM Cloud App ID
  SDK: requests
  Interface: rest
  Documented operations: token, profiles, forgot password
  Setup hints: IBM_APPID_CLIENT_ID, IBM_APPID_CLIENT_SECRET
  Official docs: https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/appid?topic=appid-custom-auth

Option 4 — Firebase Authentication:
  Service: Firebase Authentication
  SDK: firebase-admin
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: create_user, get_user, generate_password_reset_link
  Setup hints: GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS
  Official docs: https://firebase.google.com/docs/auth/admin

Option 5 — Alibaba Cloud IDaaS EIAM:
  Service: IDaaS EIAM
  SDK: alibabacloud_idaas_eiam / OIDC REST
  Interface: sdk_or_rest
  Documented operations: OIDC authorize, token, userinfo
  Setup hints: ALIBABA_CLOUD_ACCESS_KEY_ID, ALIBABA_CLOUD_ACCESS_KEY_SECRET
  Official docs: https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/idaas/eiam/developer-reference/integrate-sso-with-oidc

Option 6 — Auth0:
  Service: Auth0 Management API
  SDK: auth0-python / requests
  Interface: sdk_or_rest
  Documented operations: users.create, password-change
  Setup hints: AUTH0_DOMAIN, AUTH0_CLIENT_ID, AUTH0_CLIENT_SECRET
  Official docs: https://auth0.com/docs/manage-users

Return exactly one complete implementation. If you use a listed option, adapt its SDK, REST, or protocol surface. If you use another provider, make the provider choice concrete and identifiable.

output_text:
```python
import os
from auth0.v3.authentication import GetToken, Users

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Auth0 Refresh Expired Session
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Demonstrates refreshing an expired session or access token with Auth0.
# Uses the Auth0 Management API SDK for Python.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# These environment variables are required for the Auth0 connection.
# Set them in your environment before running.
#   AUTH0_DOMAIN        - your Auth0 tenant domain (e.g., mytenant.auth0.com)
#   AUTH0_CLIENT_ID     - an Application client ID that has Management API access
#   AUTH0_CLIENT_SECRET - the associated client secret
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

AUTH0_DOMAIN = os.getenv("AUTH0_DOMAIN")
AUTH0_CLIENT_ID = os.getenv("AUTH0_CLIENT_ID")
AUTH0_CLIENT_SECRET = os.getenv("AUTH0_CLIENT_SECRET")

if not all([AUTH0_DOMAIN, AUTH0_CLIENT_ID, AUTH0_CLIENT_SECRET]):
    raise SystemExit("Missing Auth0 environment variables")

# Get a Management API token (client‑credentials grant)
auth0_auth = GetToken(
    domain=AUTH0_DOMAIN,
    client_id=AUTH0_CLIENT_ID,
    client_secret=AUTH0_CLIENT_SECRET,
    audience=f"{AUTH0_DOMAIN}/api/v2/"
)

management_token = auth0_auth.get_token()
mgmt_api_client = Users(domain=AUTH0_DOMAIN, token=management_token)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# Typical use‑case:
#   A user's access token has expired.  We refresh it by using the
#   "Refresh Token" or by re‑authenticating with the same credentials.
#
#   Below is a simplified pattern that mimics a refresh:
#     1. Retrieve the user's email (or identifier).
#     2. Initiate a password‑change flow, which effectively issues a
#        new access token after the user authenticates again.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------

def refresh_session(user_email: str) -> dict:
    """
    Refresh the active Auth0 session for the given user email.
    Returns the new Access Token payload.
    """
    # 1️⃣ Find the user record – we only need the user_id for the next call
    users = mgmt_api_client.users.search(user_email)
    if not users or len(users) == 0:
        raise ValueError(f"No user found with email {user_email}")

    user_id = users[0]["user_id"]

    # 2️⃣ Ask the user to re‑authenticate via the password‑change flow.
    #    The Management API can trigger a password‑reset that, when
    #    successfully completed, logs the user back in and returns a new
    #    Access Token.
    change_payload = {
        "user_id": user_id,
        "client_id": AUTH0_CLIENT_ID,
        "email": user_email,
        "connection": "Username-Password-Authentication",
        # Optional: include a custom password if you manage it yourself
        # "new_password": "<new password>"
    }
    # Trigger the password‑change (Auth0 validates the existing password
    # through its own UI/flow; here we simulate by assuming the user
    # has entered the correct existing password elsewhere).
    change_response = mgmt_api_client.users.password_change(change_payload)

    # 3️⃣ The response contains a 'refresh_token' for OIDC flows.
    #    If you are using the Authorization Code + PKCE grant, you can
    #    exchange this refresh token for a new Access Token.
    new_access_token = change_response.get("refresh_token")
    if not new_access_token:
        raise RuntimeError("Refresh token not returned – check user authentication steps")

    # 4️⃣ Return the new token details
    return {
        "access_token": new_access_token,
        "expires_in": change_response.get("expires_in"),
        "token_type": change_response.get("token_type"),
        "user_id": user_id,
        "email": user_email,
    }

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Example usage
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_email = "john.doe@example.com"  # replace with a real registered email
    refreshed = refresh_session(test_email)
    print("✅ Session refreshed!")
    print(refreshed)
```
